components.description: Motivation: sensitive attributes warp manifold geometry, not just distributions, and existing fairness alignment is insufficient.

nodes.name: Standard fairness treats data as static points
nodes.description: Standard fairness approaches often treat data as static points in high-dimensional space, ignoring the underlying generative structure.

nodes.name: Sensitive attributes causally warp geometry
nodes.description: Sensitive attributes do not merely shift data distributions but causally warp the geometry of the data manifold itself.

nodes.name: Distributional alignment insufficient
nodes.description: Distributional alignment (matching P(Z|do(A=a)) across a) is often insufficient for complex data manifolds where A also affects correlation structure and variance.

nodes.name: Warped Swiss Roll illustration
nodes.description: In the Warped Swiss Roll problem, one group resides on a tightly coiled manifold and another on a loose one, illustrating structural warping beyond mean shift.

nodes.name: Naive latent alignment fails geometrically
nodes.description: A model that aligns points in latent space can map distinct geometries to the same region without correcting the underlying structural warping, yielding representations that are statistically indistinguishable but geometrically unfaithful.

components.description: CMF's proposed reframing of fairness as geometric invariance.

nodes.name: Fairness as geometric invariance
nodes.description: A representation is truly fair only if the geometry of the mapping from latent space to data space is invariant to the sensitive attribute.

nodes.name: Penalize metric tensor differences
nodes.description: CMF enforces geometric invariance by penalizing differences in the Pullback Metric Tensor (first-order geometry) of the decoder between factual and counterfactual pairs.

nodes.name: Penalize Hessian differences
nodes.description: CMF enforces geometric invariance by penalizing differences in the Hessian (second-order geometry) of the decoder between factual and counterfactual pairs.

nodes.name: Rules of latent space preserved
nodes.description: By enforcing constraints on the Jacobian and Hessian of the decoder, CMF ensures that distances and shapes in the latent space are preserved across demographic groups.

components.description: Gap in related work that CMF fills.

nodes.name: Counterfactual fairness assumes fixed geometry
nodes.description: Counterfactual fairness and related SCM-based extensions encode fairness constraints at the level of predictions or representations, assuming a fixed geometry of the latent space.

nodes.name: Fairness enforced via statistical dependencies only
nodes.description: These approaches ensure fairness primarily by controlling statistical dependencies rather than geometric or structural ones.

nodes.name: Fair representation learning uses flat Euclidean embeddings
nodes.description: Fair representation learning methods typically treat embeddings as flat Euclidean spaces and evaluate fairness via prediction invariance or statistical independence, not geometric structure.

nodes.name: Geometric deep learning studies geometry, not fairness
nodes.description: Work on Riemannian VAEs and geometry-aware generative models studies latent geometry as an inherent property of generative models, not as an object regularized for fairness under sensitive-attribute interventions.

nodes.name: No prior work enforces geometric invariance under intervention
nodes.description: To the authors' knowledge, no prior work examines how interventions on sensitive variables should preserve local geometric properties such as curvature, metric tensors, or geodesic flows.

nodes.name: CMF fills this gap
nodes.description: CMF introduces a fairness criterion assessed at the level of geometric invariance rather than statistical independence or causal effects alone, unifying SCMs, differential geometry, and fair representation learning.

components.description: Causal setup: SCM formalization and the representation-recovery goal.

nodes.name: SCM with invertible mechanism
nodes.description: An SCM is assumed where observed features X are generated by an invertible mechanism from exogenous noise U and sensitive attribute A: X = f(U, A).

nodes.name: A warps manifestation of intrinsic U
nodes.description: U represents intrinsic individual properties (e.g., talent, health), while A acts as a parameter that warps the manifestation of U into X.

nodes.name: Goal: recover A-invariant representation
nodes.description: The representation-learning goal is to recover a representation z approximately equal to U that is invariant to A.

components.description: Geometric definitions: metric tensor and Hessian as first- and second-order invariance constraints.

nodes.name: Decoder defines a smooth manifold
nodes.description: An encoder-decoder (autoencoder) framework is used where the decoder D: Z -> X defines a smooth manifold M embedded in X.

nodes.name: Pullback metric tensor defined via Jacobian
nodes.description: The geometry of the latent space is characterized by the Pullback Metric Tensor G(z) = J_D(z)^T J_D(z), measuring how infinitesimal distances scale under the decoder map.

nodes.name: Fair representation implies matched metric tensors
nodes.description: If the representation is fair, local manifold scaling should not depend on A, i.e., G(z_factual) ≈ G(z_counterfactual).

nodes.name: Metric tensor only captures first-order stretching
nodes.description: The metric tensor only captures first-order local linearities (stretching), motivating a second-order extension to capture bending and twisting.

nodes.name: Hessian defined dimension-wise
nodes.description: Since the decoder is vector-valued, the curvature constraint is defined dimension-wise via the Hessian H_k(z) = ∇²D_k(z) for each output dimension k.

components.description: Loss function construction combining task, alignment, and geometric terms.

nodes.name: Combined training loss
nodes.description: The model is trained to minimize L = L_task + L_align + λ_geo · L_geo, combining reconstruction/prediction loss, counterfactual alignment, and geometric regularization.

nodes.name: L_align is standard counterfactual alignment
nodes.description: L_align = ||E(x) - E(xcf)||^2 enforces standard counterfactual alignment of encoder outputs.

nodes.name: L_geo penalizes metric and curvature differences
nodes.description: L_geo is the novel contribution, combining the Frobenius-norm difference of metric tensors and a weighted sum of Frobenius-norm differences of per-dimension Hessians between factual and counterfactual latents.

nodes.name: do(A) enforced as isometry
nodes.description: Minimizing L_geo forces the model to learn a representation where the causal intervention do(A) acts as an isometry (preserving distances and shapes), not merely a translation.

components.description: Experimental setup: synthetic Warped Swiss Roll SCM used to validate CMF.

nodes.name: Warped Swiss Roll SCM constructed
nodes.description: A synthetic SCM is constructed with A in {0,1} and U ~ Uniform(0,4π), where observed features X in R^3 are generated via a frequency/radius parameter w = 1.0 + 0.5A.

nodes.name: A controls tightness/twist of manifold
nodes.description: The construction creates a manifold that is tighter and more twisted when A = 1, directly instantiating causal geometric warping by the sensitive attribute.

nodes.name: Ground-truth geometry known
nodes.description: The synthetic dataset is used because the ground-truth geometry is known, enabling direct evaluation of geometric invariance.

nodes.name: ELU chosen for C² continuity
nodes.description: ELU activations are used instead of ReLU because they are twice-differentiable (C² continuous), which is required for stable Hessian computation.

components.description: Quantitative results: geometric invariance and fairness-utility trade-off.

nodes.name: Baseline exhibits high geometric error
nodes.description: The Baseline autoencoder exhibits extremely high geometric errors (Metric Error 16.39, Curvature Error 4.32).

nodes.name: Baseline relies on A to reconstruct warped manifold
nodes.description: The high baseline geometric error confirms that the standard autoencoder learns to rely on the sensitive attribute A to reconstruct the warped manifold.

nodes.name: CMF reduces metric error ~1000x
nodes.description: CMF reduces the Metric Error to 0.018, an approximately 1000x reduction relative to baseline.

nodes.name: CMF reduces curvature error ~100x
nodes.description: CMF reduces the Curvature Error to 0.046, an approximately 100x reduction relative to baseline.

nodes.name: CMF achieves geometric invariance
nodes.description: The large reductions in metric and curvature error demonstrate that CMF successfully creates a representation geometrically invariant to A.

nodes.name: Accuracy drops negligibly
nodes.description: Despite heavy geometric regularization, classification accuracy drops only negligibly from 1.000 (Baseline) to 0.995 (CMF).

nodes.name: Intrinsic variable U preserved
nodes.description: The negligible accuracy drop proves that the intrinsic variable U, which predicts Y, was preserved by CMF's representation.

nodes.name: Reconstruction MSE increases
nodes.description: Reconstruction MSE increases from 0.070 (Baseline) to 0.754 (CMF), reflecting the cost of not using A as a reconstruction shortcut.

nodes.name: MSE increase reflects necessary compromise
nodes.description: The MSE increase is expected: the Baseline 'cheats' by using A to perfectly reconstruct the warped data, while CMF must find a compromise manifold fitting both demographic groups without encoding the warping factor.

nodes.name: Fairness-utility trade-off quantified
nodes.description: Together, the near-perfect fairness metrics with only a negligible accuracy drop and a moderate MSE increase quantify CMF's fairness-utility trade-off.

nodes.name: Baseline latent space separated by A
nodes.description: The Baseline latent space visualization is sharply divided by the sensitive attribute A (shown as Red/Blue clusters).

nodes.name: CMF latent space aligns distributions
nodes.description: The CMF latent space visualization shows distributions overlapping across A while preserving intrinsic structure U.

nodes.name: Alignment does not destroy causal information
nodes.description: The high accuracy score alongside distributional overlap confirms that CMF's alignment did not destroy the causal information required for prediction.

nodes.name: Contribution 1: geometric invariance formalization
nodes.description: Fairness is formalized as a geometric invariance problem requiring stability of the Riemannian metric and curvature under causal intervention.

nodes.name: Contribution 2: differentiable Jacobian/Hessian alignment loss
nodes.description: A differentiable loss function is proposed that aligns the Jacobian and Hessian of the generator across counterfactual worlds.

nodes.name: Contribution 3: GIE validation on nonlinear SCM
nodes.description: CMF is experimentally validated on a non-linear SCM, introducing Geometric Invariance Error (GIE) metrics to quantify disentanglement of structural bias.

isolated_nodes.name: Future work: approximate Hessian-vector products
isolated_nodes.description: Future work will scale CMF to high-dimensional image data using approximate Hessian-vector products to bypass the computational cost of full Hessian calculation.

isolated_nodes.name: Future work: graph-structured data
isolated_nodes.description: Future work will extend the CMF framework to graph-structured data.
